jp: あ、先生[せんせい]{が|ga-subject}来[き]ました。
en: Oh, the teacher has arrived.
why: The teacher's arrival is fresh news you are pointing out, so the subject takes が.

jp: ほら、教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}窓[まど]{が|ga-subject}開[あ]いています{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: Look, the classroom window is open.
why: You are drawing attention to what you see, so the thing observed takes が.

jp: もうすぐ授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-subject}始[はじ]まります。
en: Class is about to start.
why: An event about to happen is reported as news, and with intransitive 始まる the thing that begins takes が.

jp: 休[やす]み時間[じかん]{に|ni-time}、教室[きょうしつ]{で|de-place}生徒[せいと]{が|ga-subject}歌[うた]っていました。
en: During the break, students were singing in the classroom.
why: The students are the new subject of what was going on, so they take が.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{で|de-place}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-subject}勉強[べんきょう]しています。
en: Students are studying in the next room.
why: You report what is happening in the next room, so the doers are marked with が.

jp: やっと会議[かいぎ]{が|ga-subject}終[お]わりました。
en: The meeting has finally ended.
why: You announce the event that just happened, so the meeting, the thing that ended, takes が.

jp: 今朝[けさ]、会社[かいしゃ]{に|ni-destination}電話[でんわ]{が|ga-subject}かかってきました。
en: This morning a phone call came to the office.
why: A call that comes in is a new event, and its subject takes が.

jp: 今[いま]、廊下[ろうか]{を|o-path}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-subject}走[はし]っています。
en: A student is running along the corridor right now.
why: The runner is new information in a scene you are describing, so it takes が.

jp: コピー機[き]{が|ga-subject}故障[こしょう]しています。
en: The copy machine is broken.
why: You report a problem with the machine as news, so the subject takes が.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}電気[でんき]{が|ga-subject}急[きゅう]に消[き]えました。
en: The classroom lights suddenly went out.
why: A sudden event happens to the lights, so they are the subject marked with が.

jp: パソコン{が|ga-subject}動[うご]かなくなりました。
en: The computer stopped working.
why: The computer is the thing that changed state, so it takes が.

jp: 試験[しけん]{の|no-possessive}結果[けっか]{が|ga-subject}今日[きょう]出[で]ました。
en: The exam results came out today.
why: The results are what came out, so they are the subject marked with が.

jp: 生徒[せいと]{が|ga-subject}五人[ごにん]遅刻[ちこく]しました。
en: Five students were late.
why: You report who was late as news, so the subject takes が.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]、うち{の|no-possessive}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}留学生[りゅうがくせい]{が|ga-subject}来[き]ます。
en: Next month an exchange student will come to our school.
why: The student's arrival is new information, so the subject takes が.

jp: 明日[あした]、誰[だれ]{が|ga-subject}大阪[おおさか]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きますか。
en: Who is going to Osaka tomorrow?
why: A question word such as 誰 can never be the topic, so as the subject it must take が.

jp: 先週[せんしゅう]、山田[やまだ]さん{が|ga-subject}会社[かいしゃ]{を|o-departure}辞[や]めました。
en: Last week Ms. Yamada quit the company.
why: News about who quit presents the person as the subject with が.

jp: 窓[まど]{の|no-possessive}外[そと]{で|de-place}鳥[とり]{が|ga-subject}鳴[な]いています。
en: Birds are singing outside the window.
why: The birds are what you hear and notice, so they take が.

jp: 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]{の|no-possessive}あと、急[きゅう]に雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]ってきました。
en: After lunch it suddenly started to rain.
why: Rain that starts is a new event, so 雨 takes が.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{で|de-place}友達[ともだち]{が|ga-subject}待[ま]っています。
en: A friend is waiting in front of the library.
why: The friend is introduced as the one waiting, so the subject takes が.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}エレベーター{が|ga-subject}止[と]まりました。
en: The elevator in the office building stopped.
why: The elevator is the thing that stopped, so it takes が.

jp: 学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{で|de-place}工事[こうじ]{が|ga-subject}始[はじ]まりました。

why: The construction is the new event that began, so it takes が.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{の|no-possessive}資料[しりょう]{が|ga-subject}まだ届[とど]いていません。
en: The meeting materials have not arrived yet.
why: The materials are what has not arrived, so they are the subject marked with が.

jp: 四月[しがつ]{に|ni-time}新[あたら]しい社員[しゃいん]{が|ga-subject}三人[さんにん]入[はい]ります。
en: Three new employees will join in April.
why: A subject followed by a number (三人) reports new information and takes が, not は.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}席[せき]{の|no-possessive}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-subject}急[きゅう]に立[た]ちました。
en: The student in the next seat suddenly stood up.
why: The student who stood up is the new subject, so it takes が.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{の|no-possessive}ベル{が|ga-subject}鳴[な]りました。
en: The class bell rang.
why: A bell that rings is a sound you notice, so it takes が.

jp: 窓[まど]{から|kara-from}風[かぜ]{が|ga-subject}入[はい]ってきます。
en: The wind is coming in through the window.
why: The wind is what you feel coming in, so it is marked with が.

jp: 会議室[かいぎしつ]{の|no-possessive}ドア{が|ga-subject}開[あ]きました。
en: The door of the meeting room opened.
why: The door opened by itself, so it is the subject of 開く and takes が.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]{から|kara-from}、会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}ルール{が|ga-subject}変[か]わります。
en: From next month the company's rules will change.
why: The rules are what changes, so they are the subject marked with が.

jp: 昨日[きのう]、教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}時計[とけい]{が|ga-subject}止[と]まりました。
en: Yesterday the clock in the classroom stopped.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{の|no-possessive}お母[かあ]さん{が|ga-subject}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}来[き]ました。
en: A friend's mother came to the school.
why: The visitor is reported as new information, so the subject takes が.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]{が|ga-subject}病気[びょうき]{で|de-cause}休[やす]んでいます。
en: A colleague is absent because of illness.
why: You report who is absent as news, so the subject takes が.

jp: 木村[きむら]さん{が|ga-subject}大学[だいがく]{を|o-departure}卒業[そつぎょう]したこと{を|o-object}聞[き]きました。
en: I heard that Mr. Kimura graduated from university.
why: Inside a clause that describes こと, the subject takes が; は cannot be used there.

jp: 今日[きょう]、新[あたら]しい学生[がくせい]{が|ga-subject}教室[きょうしつ]{に/へ|ni-destination}入[はい]ってきました。
en: Today a new student came into the classroom.
why: A newcomer entering is a new event, so the subject takes が.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{が|ga-subject}階段[かいだん]{で|de-place}転[ころ]びました。
en: Mr. Tanaka fell down on the stairs.
why: An accident happening to a person is reported with the person as が subject.

jp: 父[ちち]{の|no-possessive}会社[かいしゃ]{が|ga-subject}引[ひ]っ越[こ]しました。
en: My father's company has moved.
why: The company is what moved, so it is the subject marked with が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{が|ga-subject}教室[きょうしつ]{から/を|kara-from}出[で]ていきました。
en: The teacher went out of the classroom.
why: The teacher is the one who left, reported as an event, so が marks the subject.

jp: 午後[ごご]二時[にじ]{から/に|kara-from}会議室[かいぎしつ]{で|de-place}会議[かいぎ]{が|ga-subject}始[はじ]まります。
en: A meeting starts in the meeting room at two in the afternoon.
why: The meeting is the thing that begins, so it takes が.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}新[あたら]しい大学[だいがく]{が|ga-subject}できました。
en: A new university has opened near the station.
why: The new university is what came into being, so it takes が.

jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{の|no-possessive}辞書[じしょ]{が|ga-subject}落[お]ちました。
en: The dictionary on the desk fell.
why: The dictionary is what fell, so it is the subject marked with が.

jp: 先月[せんげつ]、会社[かいしゃ]{に|ni-destination}新[あたら]しいパソコン{が|ga-subject}届[とど]きました。
en: Last month a new computer arrived at the office.
why: The computer is what arrived, so it takes が.

jp: 昼休[ひるやす]み{に|ni-time}、食堂[しょくどう]{で|de-place}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-subject}倒[たお]れました。
en: At lunch break a student collapsed in the cafeteria.
why: A student collapsing is a sudden event, so the person takes が.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に/で|ni-location}タクシー{が|ga-subject}止[と]まりました。
en: A taxi stopped in front of the office.
why: The taxi is what stopped, so it takes が.

jp: 新[あたら]しい部長[ぶちょう]{が|ga-subject}やっと決[き]まりました。
en: The new department head has finally been decided.
why: You report what has just been settled as news, so the subject of 決まる takes が.

jp: この学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}留学生[りゅうがくせい]{が|ga-subject}増[ふ]えました。
en: The number of exchange students at this school has increased.
why: The exchange students are what increased, so they take が.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{の|no-possessive}時間[じかん]{が|ga-subject}変[か]わりました。
en: The meeting time has changed.
why: The meeting time is what changed, so it takes が.

jp: 運動場[うんどうじょう]{で|de-place}生徒[せいと]{が|ga-subject}サッカー{を|o-object}しています。
en: Students are playing soccer on the sports field.
why: You describe a scene you can see, so the people doing the action take が.

jp: 今朝[けさ]、学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{で|de-place}事故[じこ]{が|ga-subject}起[お]きました。
en: This morning an accident happened in front of the school.
why: The accident is a new event that took place, so it takes が.
